annotation.interpretation_a: The implementation must track the state transition to SYN-RECEIVED regardless of whether it was initiated by a passive or active open.
annotation.interpretation_b: The implementation must track the *source* of the SYN-RECEIVED state transition (passive vs. active) in addition to the state itself.
annotation.justification: The clause states that a TCP implementation "MUST keep track of whether a connection has reached SYN-RECEIVED state as the result of a passive OPEN or an active OPEN." This could be interpreted as simply tracking whether the connection is in the SYN-RECEIVED state, or tracking *how* it got there (i.e., whether it was a passive or active open). The latter interpretation requires storing additional information, and is not explicitly stated.
annotation.missing_information: It is unclear whether the tracking requirement is simply to know that the connection *reached* SYN-RECEIVED, or to know *how* it reached SYN-RECEIVED. The latter would require storing additional information.
